swap.evidence: Swapped into a community seed library and a meeting-room booker: the ground, cards, green button, badges, calendar and wrench-placeholder thumbnails all survive with only words changed (the wrench would become a seed or door glyph). Bound to this product: only copy (deposits, 'Open' sessions, 14 Mill Lane, volunteer desk). With the name hidden the page reads as 'some booking catalogue', because the thumbnails show no tools.

category_guess.evidence: Predicted default for a community lending/booking service: light neutral ground, one green community accent, white bordered cards with icon thumbnails, availability pills, month calendar of open days. Predicted opposite: dark poster-like look with heavy display type. Ground, accent, cards, thumbnails, pills and calendar all match the default.

similar_prompt.evidence: Brief: 'online reservation for a volunteer-run kit library in a village hall'. Predicted choices: green accent, card grid with icon placeholders, availability badges, calendar with open days, single-column forms. Overlap is near total; nothing here was driven by Fernhill's own world (the membership card, the room, the tool tags).

mode_fit: All five surfaces are Operate/Read and the design keeps them conventional and quiet, which is correct; no hero moments, no choreography. The shortfall is the identity floor (mark, imagery, the library's own material), not missing expression.

detector_comparison.notes: Detectors returned no hits. Possible SLP-28 (emerald/teal sole accent) would be exempt here: DESIGN.md ties the green to the membership card and it also carries availability semantics. Nothing from the detectors would have changed either verdict.

findings.title: Every tool card shows the same wrench placeholder instead of the tool
findings.description: On Find a tool all ten cards carry an identical mint square with the same wrench glyph. The thumbnail slot takes about a fifth of each card but carries no information: a ladder, a pressure washer and a hedge trimmer look the same, and the page reads as an unfilled template.
findings.impact: Members scanning for 'the drill with two batteries' may have to read every title because the image gives no recognition cue; the placeholder on show is likely to make the library look unfinished at first view.
findings.recommendation: Decide what the thumbnail is for: real photographs of the library's own items (the brief says one of each), or a per-category drawn glyph set, or remove the slot so the name leads.

findings.title: No identity beyond the name in bold body text; the membership-card green is not carried as a mark
findings.description: The masthead is a small wrench icon and 'Fernhill Tool Library' in bold text at body size. DESIGN.md names the membership card's green as the source of the palette, but the green appears only on buttons and badges. Nothing from the library's world (card, room, tool tags, session sheet) appears on any surface.
findings.impact: 'Neighbourly' is carried only by copy; first-time members may not recognise this as their local library's service rather than a generic booking site.

evidence.detail: no designed mark or product-world element on find, tool, basket, confirm or done

findings.recommendation: Decide one identity element taken from the library's own material (for example the membership card) and carry it quietly on every surface, within the Operate budget.

findings.title: Filter panel uses unthemed browser-default date and select controls
findings.description: Opening filters reveals a native date input showing 'yyyy/mm/dd' and a native select with its own chevron; the 'Category' label sits lower than 'Available from', so the two controls do not share a baseline.
findings.impact: The date format contradicts the brief's 'Saturday 17 October' convention and may confuse en-GB members; the controls look unlike the rest of the system.
findings.recommendation: Decide whether the filter needs a free date at all (sessions are a short list); style the controls with the system's input tokens and align labels.

findings.title: On phones the search sits below all ten tool cards
findings.description: At 375 the 'Search tools' field and filter button appear after the full list, just above Opening times, while at 768+ they sit above the list.
findings.impact: On the main device (phones), the tool for the surface's single job is the last thing a member reaches; members looking for one tool may scroll the list first.
findings.recommendation: Keep the same order at all widths, or record why phones differ.

findings.title: Tool names truncate with ellipses on phones, making the two drills indistinguishable
findings.description: At 375 card titles are cut to one line: 'Cordless drill 18 V, co...' appears twice, and 'Extension ladder 3 m ...', 'Hedge trimmer, cord...' lose the distinguishing detail.
findings.impact: The distinguishing part of the name (two batteries vs one battery) is the part cut off, on the device most members use.
findings.recommendation: Let titles wrap; decide whether the thumbnail earns its width on phones.

findings.title: Tool details are two lists with different label column widths
findings.description: Category / Deposit / Available from set values at x≈224, while Chuck / Batteries / Weight / Case set values at x≈180, directly below, with an uneven gap between the groups.
findings.impact: The ragged value column reads as careless, working against 'careful'; members comparing specs must re-find the column.
findings.recommendation: Use one label column for all details, or separate the groups with a sub-heading.

findings.title: Basket session cards: one orphaned full-width card above five cramped ones
findings.description: At 1280 'Wednesday 28 October' fills a full row on its own, while the other five sessions share one row and wrap to three lines each. Sessions are also listed latest-first.
findings.impact: The layout gives most weight to the least likely session and makes the dates hard to scan; the page looks unfinished.
findings.recommendation: Decide a session layout where every session gets equal weight and dates sit on one line, in date order.

findings.title: Footer stops short of the viewport, leaving an empty band on short pages
findings.description: On Basket and Done at 1280 the white footer ends at about y=805 and y=700 of 900, with the page ground continuing below it.
findings.impact: A band that stops for no reason is a visible sign of unfinish on the confirmation page members see last.
findings.recommendation: Make the page fill the viewport so the footer sits at the bottom.

findings.title: 'Added to your basket' toast overlaps the calendar's weekday header
findings.description: After adding, the toast appears centred over the We/Th header row of the calendar.
findings.impact: The confirmation covers part of the control the member was just using; may read as a layering slip.
findings.recommendation: Place the toast where it does not cover content, for example attached to the action bar.

findings.title: Sticky reserve bar's button sits outside the content column at wide widths
findings.description: At 1280 the 'Reserve this tool' button's right edge is at about x=1264 while the content column ends at 1184; the bar is unaligned with everything above it.
findings.impact: The page's one primary action looks detached from the page grid, a small but visible craft lapse on the key Operate screen.

evidence.detail: full-page capture also shows the fixed bar over the calendar; that overlap may be a capture artefact

findings.recommendation: Constrain the bar's content to the page's content width.

findings.title: Wide layouts leave the right half of Confirm and Done empty with no focal point
findings.description: At 1280 the details form and the 'What happens next' card occupy about 610 px of a 1088 px container; the confirmation page has no moment that marks the reservation as made beyond the H1.
findings.impact: Half-empty wide views read as an unfinished document; on Done, the member's reassurance rests on plain text alone.
findings.recommendation: Decide what the wide layout is for on these pages (a narrower centred column, or a summary beside the form) so the space is chosen rather than left over.

strengths: Copy voice is concrete and neighbourly: 'Enough for a day of fixing shelves and a fence', 'call the desk... during opening hours'.
One filled button per page and a clear error summary with linked messages on Confirm.
Dark theme is composed (lighter cards on a dark green ground, lightened accent), not inverted.
keep: Keep the volunteer-desk voice and the deposit-and-availability-on-every-card discipline.
notes: No baseline in packet, so pairwise not run (DES-05 not_applicable). Bash heredoc was denied once; files written with the Write tool. Observations for other evaluators (not design findings): day-chosen 1280-light shows Monday 12 October selected although it is not a session day; Done still shows 'Basket (1)' in the nav; the no-results capture shows the full list with 'sewing machine' typed and no empty message, possibly an unsubmitted capture. Behaviour (fades, focus, calendar keyboard) not assessable from stills.
